text: Your first sign-in. The app ships with one account: owner / 1234
The app now insists you pick your own PIN — 1234 is printed in the manual
Choose something only you know. There is no back door if you forget it
A brand-new shop. The app asks four questions before anything else
Step 1 — your shop name. This prints at the top of every bill
Step 2 — tax. Gold is already exempt, the FBR treatment
Step 3 — which gold you deal in. Skip what you never sell
Each one you keep is a rate you post every morning — so pick honestly
That is the setup. Everything else already ships set the way shops want it
Now the rate. Nothing can be priced or sold until today’s is posted
Quote it the way your market does — per tola, per gram, or per 10 grams
The whole board fills from this one figure — check it, then post
One number, one tap, every morning. That is the whole daily chore
Nothing is stored as a price. Post a new rate and every item reprices
Now your stock. Most shops already have it in Excel
Import from a spreadsheet — no need to retype hundreds of pieces
It reads your column names — "Gross Wt", "Net Wt", purity, making charge
Every row is shown BEFORE anything is saved. Nothing is written yet
Weights in tola instead of grams? Switch the unit and the preview follows
A row it cannot read is listed with the reason, and simply skipped
Happy with the preview? Import — and only now is anything written
Opening stock is posted at the same time, so your ledger starts balanced
Your catalogue — imported, and already priced at today’s rate
No price was ever typed. Weight, purity and making charge produce it
You are open for business. Ringing up the first sale
Scan the tag, or type the name and press Enter
The bill builds itself — metal, making and wastage at today’s rate
F9 finishes the sale. The receipt opens, and stock drops by one
Hand it to the customer, or Ctrl-P to print
Add your counter staff under Settings — each picks their own PIN
Backups run on their own: every 4 hours, on close, and before an upgrade
That is the setup. Post the rate each morning — the rest is selling
